items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: The reason I really could relate to it I think, I started listening to Albert Ayler you know, “Ghosts and Spirits” and all that.

ctx.x: Like Kidd Jordan down there, right?

Yes. And he kind of found that out near the end. But for most of my life I didn’t like it. People thought I couldn’t get into that and this, that and the other. But I met a clarinet player, Perry Robinson, who was from New York and he was an underground legend of the loft movement of the ‘60s and he played and recorded with a number of people in the avant garde vein. He was an older guy, and he came down to New Orleans to play. And, long story short, I sat in with him and he kept asking me to sit in. There were…

to get back to some state of normalcy, or living in the new existence. It was very painful. There were a lot of losses. I went through a plethora of emotions: bewilderment, anger, you know of being frightened, fear. Little joy here and there. And I needed to express those things. I wrote a bunch of songs at a artist’s retreat here called Studio in the Woods, A Studio in the Woods. And I recorded them on a recording called “Blue Crescent.” And the idea was it was kind of like my version of the state of New Orleans…
